risks.note: Operates in a highly competitive industry facing domestic manufacturers as well as low-cost international suppliers; increased competition may pressure pricing, margins and market share across key product categories.

Changes in trade policy, including a potential withdrawal of anti-dumping duties on imported insulators (particularly from China), may increase the influx of low-cost imports and intensify pricing pressure in the domestic market.

Demand for the Company's products is closely linked to investments in power transmission, distribution and infrastructure development; any slowdown in capital expenditure, policy implementation or project awards may impact order inflows and revenue growth.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange and interest rate risk

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for insulators is driven by expansion of India's transmission and distribution network, renewable energy evacuation infrastructure, Green Energy Corridor projects, smart grid modernisation and rising adoption of EHV/UHV transmission systems.
- Railway electrification investments are creating additional demand for specialised insulator products used in overhead equipment and traction infrastructure.
- Higher production volumes, improved capacity utilisation, better manufacturing efficiencies and a favourable product mix widened margins for the High Tension Insulators Division during the year.
- Government programmes (RDSS, National Electricity Plan, Green Energy Corridor, Make in India, PM Gati Shakti) are cited as structural demand drivers across the insulator and conductor divisions.
- A potential reduction or elimination of anti-dumping duties on imported insulators (particularly from China) is flagged as a risk that could increase low-cost imports and intensify pricing competition.
- Real estate segment profitability improved on effective asset management, prudent cost control and ongoing monetisation despite a marginal revenue decline.
- The Division maintained a healthy order pipeline as on March 31, 2026, reflecting sustained demand across domestic and export markets and providing strong revenue visibility for the coming months.
- The robust order book is described as underscoring customer confidence in the Division's product quality, execution capabilities and long-standing market presence.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Launch and execution of a major capacity expansion programme (six new kilns, ~21,780 MT/annum additional kiln loading capacity, roughly doubling existing capacity) to strengthen operational flexibility, improve delivery capability and support export growth.
- Deepen international/export market presence, having grown export sales over 175% during the year; intensified participation in global trade forums (Hannover Messe, IEEE PES T&D Chicago) and geographic diversification into North America and Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Malaysia, Philippines).
- Redevelop ageing real estate/warehouse assets into modern infrastructure to capture warehousing and logistics demand and support stable, recurring cash flows.
- Strengthen manufacturing/operational excellence via cost optimisation, improved production planning and manufacturing productivity.
- Build organisational capability through onboarding of experienced professionals across key domains and strengthening leadership depth.
- FY27 priorities: successful commissioning/stabilisation of the ongoing capacity expansion, market diversification across domestic and international customers, sustaining Insulators Division growth and market share, operational excellence, margin/return-ratio improvement, and strengthening working-capital management.
- Dividend policy is governed by a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy; the Board recommended a Final Dividend for FY26 subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, with preference shareholders entitled to dividend in priority to equity shareholders per the terms of issue. The Company did not propose any transfer to general reserves for FY26 and instead set off the accumulated deficit in Retained Earnings against the balance in General Reserves, indicating a reserve-management approach focused on balance-sheet repair alongside continued (modest) equity dividend payout.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Board approved a CAPEX project to enhance production capacity of the Insulators Plant at Mandideep from 16,500 MT to 36,000 MT, proposed to be completed by December 2026, through installation of additional kiln firing units together with auxiliary equipment (dryers, pug mills, CNC shaping machines and other supporting machinery) and expansion of the existing building structure. Separately, the Company described a kiln loading capacity increase of approximately 21,780 MT per annum through installation of six new kilns — roughly doubling existing capacity of 20,640 MT to approximately 42,420 MT. One kiln was successfully commissioned in April 2026; two additional kilns are expected to become operational in Q1 FY2026-27, with the remaining kilns commissioned in a phased manner thereafter. The investment is intended to improve production flexibility, reduce lead times and strengthen competitiveness in domestic and export markets.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over six decades of manufacturing expertise and enduring relationships with utilities, EPC contractors and infrastructure developers
- Comprehensive product portfolio spanning voltage classes from 33 kV to 765 kV
- Internationally certified manufacturing facilities and integrated quality control from raw material inspection through glazing, firing, testing and dispatch
- Broadbased, diversified customer ecosystem across the power transmission value chain, reducing dependence on any single customer category
- Growing export presence and approvals secured from several reputed government utilities for supply of disc, long rod, solid-core post and hollow insulators
- Ongoing capacity expansion expected to more than double manufacturing capacity, improving flexibility and lead times

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Market competition risk — Operates in a highly competitive industry facing domestic manufacturers as well as low-cost international suppliers; increased competition may pressure pricing, margins and market share across key product categories.
- Trade policy and import risk — Changes in trade policy, including a potential withdrawal of anti-dumping duties on imported insulators (particularly from China), may increase the influx of low-cost imports and intensify pricing pressure in the domestic market.
- Power sector cyclicality risk — Demand for the Company's products is closely linked to investments in power transmission, distribution and infrastructure development; any slowdown in capital expenditure, policy implementation or project awards may impact order inflows and revenue growth.
- Raw material and energy cost risk — Operations depend on key raw materials such as metals, ceramic inputs and energy resources; volatility in commodity prices, fuel costs and power tariffs may increase manufacturing costs and impact profitability.
- Project execution and customer delay risk — Delays in project execution, funding constraints, approval processes or payment delays at customer organisations - particularly government agencies and public sector undertakings - may affect order execution schedules, receivable cycles and working capital requirements.
- Liquidity and working capital risk — Extended project cycles, delayed customer payments and fluctuations in order execution schedules may increase working capital requirements and impact liquidity management.
- Foreign exchange and interest rate risk — Exposure to foreign currency fluctuations from export transactions and imports of raw materials, plus interest-rate changes, may impact financing costs and profitability.
- Environment, health and safety (EHS) risk — Manufacturing operations involve exposure to occupational health, safety and environmental risks; non-compliance with EHS standards may lead to accidents, operational disruptions, regulatory actions and reputational impact.
